findings.what: The cross-context CAS-convergence assertion `await expect(page.getByTestId("firm-setup-stale")).toBeVisible();` relies on Playwright's unmodified default 5000ms timeout, immediately after a sequence the file's own comment (`test.describe.configure({ timeout: 180_000 })`, lines ~70-73) says is 'measured, ~32s on this host' because two full sign-ins and two server renders live inside the cell. The per-assertion timeout was never widened to match that documented margin.
findings.evidence: Independently re-ran the isolated spec (dedicated ports 3290/3291/3292, no reset flags) three times this session: run 1 timed out at browser launch (`browserContext.addCookies` after 180s — a pre-app-code CDP hang, host had 126 node/chrome processes at the time); run 2 (clean) passed cells 1 (11.3s) and 2 (20.9s) then failed exactly at this assertion (`element(s) not found`, 5000ms timeout) with cells 4-5 not run; run 3 (full retry) stalled again under escalating contention (114-130 processes) and did not conclude inside this review's window. The underlying SQL CAS mechanism itself is proven correct independently and repeatably: `p648.answer.stale` in packages/db/tests/firm-setup.test.mjs passed 15/15 against real Postgres, and the client's `submit` closure (firm-setup-checklist.tsx:166-192) carries a captured `env.revision_token` with no auto-refetch (no focus/visibilitychange/poll listener found in lib/firm/use-async-read.ts) that would silently absorb the conflict, so nothing found here implicates the application/door logic — this reads as a testing-robustness gap under this host's documented 12-lane contention, not a functional defect.
findings.fix: Widen the timeout on this specific assertion (e.g. `.toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 })`) or set a per-file/per-test `expect: { timeout }` override in the same place the test already widens the overall test timeout for this cell, so a slow-but-correct convergence isn't reported as a missing one. Re-verify once host contention is lower; do not change the CAS/door logic itself.

findings.what: The binding brief and DECISIONS.md both state 'Firm intake documents link to #633's `(firm)/documents` leaf... If #633 has not merged, render an honest named line, not a dead href, and say so.' #633 has not merged into this branch (no `(firm)/documents` route exists), and the shipped #648 diff contains zero references to firm intake documents anywhere in the web or db surface — no link, no honest placeholder line. The final report (reports/648-final.md) never mentions #633 or this decision item, unlike its explicit, careful treatment of every other N/A/deferred brief item (Runtime: none, Successor: none owed, D10 residuals, etc.).
findings.evidence: `grep -rn -i "intake\|supporting doc\|unassigned.doc\|uploaded" apps/web/components/firm-setup/ apps/web/lib/firm-setup/ apps/web/app/(firm)/settings/setup/ packages/db/migrations/0203_firm_setup.sql` returns nothing; `find apps/web/app/(firm)/documents` (the #633 leaf) does not exist on this branch; reports/648-final.md has no '633' occurrence.
findings.fix: Not a functional gap (no AC or TDD seam in brief §3/§4 actually requires a documents reference, since the shipped catalogue is all typed text/choice/month/labelled_object with no file evidence), but the report should have closed the loop explicitly, e.g. one line: 'no firm-intake-document reference exists in this slice's twelve catalogue items, so brief item 17 is N/A here' — for a reader following the binding brief line-by-line.
